1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and Raja Babu Gupta, who appears for the informant.
2. The accused-applicant seeks bail in FIR/Case Crime No.0186 of 2020 under section 376 & 506 IPC and section 3 & 4 POCSO Act, P.S. Malhipur, District Shravasti.

3. In terms of the FIR lodged through an application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C. it was alleged that the relative of the informant had died because of which, the informant as well as her husband and two children had gone to the village.
Subsequently, the sister in law and the brother in law of the informant came and when they saw she was alone and sister in law went washroom, then the applicant committed wrong on her.

4. The counsel for the applicant argues that similar FIR was lodged by the same informant against the applicants in a different district Bahraich in which the final report was filed against which the protest petition was also filed, which is pending.
It is further stated that the informant and the applicant had performed Nikah at Mumbai and on account of the matrimonial family dispute, this false FIR has been lodged.
The tentative age of the victim is around 23 years.

5. Considering the victim to be major and similar FIR has been lodged at her instance at two places,
a clear case for bail is made out, more so when the applicant is in custody since 16.09.2025 and has no criminal history.
Thus the bail application is allowed.
